newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges up on bunker demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges up on bunker demand.

text.p: European fuel oil barges moved up on Tuesday, with some traders saying bunker demand seemed to be picking up and supplies were tight, but others dismissed the higher prices as not reflecting the market fundamentals.

Heavy sulphur barges were reported traded at $87 a tonne fob Rotterdam, against Monday's highest deal at $1 a tonne lower, and earlier they traded at $85.50 and $86. "Bunker demand is now coming in and supplies are tight," one trader said.
Traders said that the bid/offer range continued in the $86.50/$87 area after the earlier five or six deals.
But some said Tuesday's higher prices were manipulated by traders wanting to push the market higher and were not linked to the supply-demand picture.

"There is really not that much bunker demand but people are interested in manipulating the prices to the upside because it favours their positions...There is only 10,000 tonnes demand," one trader said.
No deals were heard in the high sulphur cargoes market with traders saying that players were still cautious after Monday's trade at $81.75 fob Coryton.

Supplies were reported to be tight as swaps moved into backwardation. One trader said sellers were now asking in the early eighties. Several traders said they were puzzled at the price the cargo fetched, adding that the few buyers out there were waiting for the levels to come down soon. "It is puzzling as to why that cargo traded at the level it did. A lot of people are sitting on the fence at the moment as they believe the levels will come down definitely," a trader said.
